description_en: A stone memorial pillar from circa 13th-16th century.The pillar is located in the village of Dansangu, 2.5 km east of Khalaṅgā (Jumla Bajār). It is installed in front of a small circular temple dedicated to Gaṇeśa.The pillar consists in a stone slab with a rounded top. The two sides of the pillar are oriented east and west. The west side of the pillar has eroded carvings. The top part contains a central circular motif. Below it is a vertical line that divides the pillar in two vertical sections. On the eastern side it is possible to discern engraved Nāgarī characters of an eroded inscription. The inscription appears to have entirely covered this side of the pillar.Stone memorial pillars were erected throughout the Karnali Basin from the 13th to the 17th centuries. They were erected to honour war heroes (Andolfatto 2019). It is currently impossible to decipher the inscription on the eastern side but the pillar's typology suggests that it was erected between the 13th and 16th centuries.The Gaṇeśa temple is a relatively recent construction (20th century), built with stone and mud masonry. A cemented platform has been added round the monument. The roof consists of sheet metal plates. Inside the nearby Gaṇeśa temple is a stone image of the god (JUM0170-001) from circa 19th-20th century.
monument_assessment: Good (very few light surface damages, renovated or repaired)
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. 2019. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne Université.
